\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Compute the Lanczos approximation \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat y} to \AtlasInlineMath{h(A)b} in the specified floating-point model.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
Assume \AtlasInlineMath{A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}} with spectrum in \AtlasInlineMath{[a,b_{\mathrm{spec}}]}, \AtlasInlineMath{\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\Lambda}, and \AtlasInlineMath{b\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}}. The function \AtlasInlineMath{h} satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{|h(x)|\le C_h} on the extended interval \AtlasInlineMath{[a-\eta,b_{\mathrm{spec}}+\eta]}, where \AtlasInlineMath{0<\eta\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
Spectral bounds, \AtlasInlineMath{h,b,\Lambda,\eta,C_h}, and the target error are public. Floating-point operations follow the source relative-rounding model with unit roundoff \AtlasInlineMath{u} and no overflow or underflow. Products satisfy \AtlasInlineMath{\|\operatorname{fl}(Av)-Av\|_2\le2d^{3/2}\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2u} for each vector; exact \AtlasInlineMath{Av} is not supplied.

A public scalar-function interface evaluates \AtlasInlineMath{h(x)} to relative accuracy \AtlasInlineMath{u} on the extended spectral interval: \AtlasInlineMath{|\operatorname{fl}(h(x))-h(x)|\le u|h(x)|}. This is the implementation assumption in Section 5. Count these calls separately as \AtlasInlineMath{N_h}; the running time of an expensive scalar function is not implicitly constant.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return the point \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat y\in\mathbb R^d} produced by the specified finite-precision algorithm. No separate error certificate is required.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base loss is \AtlasInlineMath{\|\widehat{y}-h(A)b\|_2/\|b\|_2} with threshold \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}. Define \AtlasInlineMath{\delta_k=\inf_{\deg q<k}\max_{x\in[a-\eta,b_{\mathrm{spec}}+\eta]}|q(x)-h(x)|}, the polynomial-approximation error in the source bound.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
The joint resource is \AtlasInlineMath{(N_{\mathrm{mv}},b_{\mathrm{fp}},N_h)}. There are at most \AtlasInlineMath{k} approximate matrix-vector products. The specified postprocessing evaluates \AtlasInlineMath{h} at at most \AtlasInlineMath{k} tridiagonal eigenvalues, hence \AtlasInlineMath{N_h\le k}. The quantity \AtlasInlineMath{b_{\mathrm{fp}}} is the effective mantissa precision for the entire run.

The three quantities remain independent resource coordinates. The source gives sufficient mantissa precision, and the scalar-function interface must additionally attain the stated relative evaluation error. Full arithmetic or bit-operation time depends on the implementation.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Use the source k-step finite-precision Lanczos algorithm with Gu-Eisenstat tridiagonal eigendecomposition. Adding full reorthogonalization changes the algorithm and its guarantee. Rounding follows Requirement 1 and the matrix-product error assumptions.

For every fixed admissible input and arithmetic error satisfying the stated rounding model, the source gives a deterministic action-error bound. There is no private randomness or success-probability parameter.

\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed worst-case joint budget; no expectation substituted
